section_1.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Briefly review the concept of a 'vector basis' (e.g., i, j, k axes). Introduce the core philosophy: any complex periodic signal can be decomposed into simple, pure sine and cosine 'building blocks'. Visualize this as a musical chord being resolved into individual notes.
section_1.example: Imagine a color: purple is actually a mixture of pure red and pure blue. Fourier series is the 'prism' that splits the signal color into its pure primary components.

section_2.title: Defining the Pure Fourier Series (0:45-1:45)
section_2.content: Present the mathematical definition: f(x) = a₀/2 + Σ(aₙ cos(nx) + bₙ sin(nx)). Explain the function of each part: the average value (a₀), and the contribution of higher-frequency ripples (aₙ, bₙ).
section_2.example: Visual animation: A circle rotating (phasor) that draws a wave. Show how changing 'n' adds high-frequency 'wiggles' to the curve.

section_3.title: Calculating Coefficients (1:45-3:15)
section_3.content: Introduce the Orthogonality Principle. Explain that we extract the specific weight of each sine/cosine by calculating the area of overlap (integral) between the signal and the basis function. Use a 'Filtering' metaphor.
section_3.example: A 'tuning fork' analogy: The integral acts like a filter that only rings when it finds the specific frequency n. If the signal doesn't contain that frequency, the overlap is zero.

section_4.title: Visual Synthesis & Application (3:15-4:30)
section_4.content: Demonstrate the 'Reconstruction'. Show an animation of a Square Wave being formed by stacking successive sine waves. As 'n' increases, the approximation gets sharper.
section_4.example: A digital synthesizer or audio equalizer: Each slider (fader) on an equalizer represents one 'aₙ' or 'bₙ' coefficient. Moving the fader changes the 'texture' of the sound wave.

section_5.title: Summary & Wrap-up (4:30-5:00)
section_5.content: Reinforce that Fourier series turns complex time-domain signals into simple frequency-domain coefficients. It is the backbone of MP3 compression, image processing (JPEG), and quantum mechanics.
section_5.example: A cat listening to a complex noise—its brain (via the cochlea) performs a Fourier transform to identify the specific purrs and meows hidden in the air pressure fluctuations.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Calculating Coefficients (1:45-3:15)", [
            "We use integrals to extract specific weights.",
            "The overlap measures how much frequency exists.",
            "Think of a filter tuning to a frequency."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        formula = MathTex(r"a_n = \frac{2}{T} \int_0^T f(t) \sin\left(\frac{2\pi n t}{T}\right) dt", color=WHITE)
        projection = VGroup(
            Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.4),
            FunctionGraph(lambda t: np.sin(t*2), x_range=[0, 4], color=RED)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

section_1.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Briefly review the concept of a 'vector basis' (e.g., i, j, k axes). Introduce the core philosophy: any complex periodic signal can be decomposed into simple, pure sine and cosine 'building blocks'. Visualize this as a musical chord being resolved into individual notes.
section_1.example: Imagine a color: purple is actually a mixture of pure red and pure blue. Fourier series is the 'prism' that splits the signal color into its pure primary components.

section_2.title: Defining the Pure Fourier Series (0:45-1:45)
section_2.content: Present the mathematical definition: f(x) = a₀/2 + Σ(aₙ cos(nx) + bₙ sin(nx)). Explain the function of each part: the average value (a₀), and the contribution of higher-frequency ripples (aₙ, bₙ).
section_2.example: Visual animation: A circle rotating (phasor) that draws a wave. Show how changing 'n' adds high-frequency 'wiggles' to the curve.

section_3.title: Calculating Coefficients (1:45-3:15)
section_3.content: Introduce the Orthogonality Principle. Explain that we extract the specific weight of each sine/cosine by calculating the area of overlap (integral) between the signal and the basis function. Use a 'Filtering' metaphor.
section_3.example: A 'tuning fork' analogy: The integral acts like a filter that only rings when it finds the specific frequency n. If the signal doesn't contain that frequency, the overlap is zero.

section_4.title: Visual Synthesis & Application (3:15-4:30)
section_4.content: Demonstrate the 'Reconstruction'. Show an animation of a Square Wave being formed by stacking successive sine waves. As 'n' increases, the approximation gets sharper.
section_4.example: A digital synthesizer or audio equalizer: Each slider (fader) on an equalizer represents one 'aₙ' or 'bₙ' coefficient. Moving the fader changes the 'texture' of the sound wave.

section_5.title: Summary & Wrap-up (4:30-5:00)
section_5.content: Reinforce that Fourier series turns complex time-domain signals into simple frequency-domain coefficients. It is the backbone of MP3 compression, image processing (JPEG), and quantum mechanics.
section_5.example: A cat listening to a complex noise—its brain (via the cochlea) performs a Fourier transform to identify the specific purrs and meows hidden in the air pressure fluctuations.
